title: God is love
hookLine: a short letter answers what God is in three words

lines: A LETTER ANSWERS IN THREE WORDS.
cards: Ask a room of people what God is, and the answers get long fast. Maker of everything. Judge.
Near the end of the New Testament there's a short letter, traditionally linked to the apostle John, that answers in three words. Not God has love, or God gives love, or God loves.
Something stranger, and harder to get out of: God is love.

teach.h: NOT GOD LOVES: GOD IS LOVE.
teach.b: In the King James, the fourth chapter of First John reads: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love." First, the shape.
The letter doesn't say love is one of God's qualities, the way a person is tall or patient. It says God is love, as if love were what God is made of, and Christian writers keep turning that over.
Second, the problem a few verses later: "No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us." The unseen God shows up where people love each other.

teach.h: WE LOVE, BECAUSE HE FIRST LOVED.
teach.b: Third, the order: "We love him, because he first loved us." Love doesn't start with us; it's received first, then passed on.

teach.h: THE TEST: THE BROTHER YOU CAN SEE.
teach.b: Fourth, the test, and it's blunt: "If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar."
If you can't love the brother you can see, the letter reasons, how would you love God, whom you can't? So the sentence isn't only a comfort. It's a measuring stick.
Whatever else a reader believes about God, in the letter's terms love isn't proven in the sky. It's proven at the kitchen table, the office, the group chat, with the person right in front of you.

how: Christians read First John in worship and private prayer, and the line God is love appears on church walls, cards and gravestones.

games.q: inside First John 4 — tap the pairs.
p: the letter calls him a liar

s: the letter says God has love, as one quality among many
it says God is love: "for God is love."
First John says nobody has seen God
"No man hath seen God at any time." the letter says God dwells where people love one another.
in the letter, love starts with us
"We love him, because he first loved us." love is received first, then passed on.

games.q: someone says, I love God, but I can't stand my brother. according to First John, what's the verdict?
games.why: the letter is blunt: he is a liar, because whoever can't love the brother he can see can't love the God he can't.

practice: Picture one ordinary moment still ahead of you today, a meeting, a meal, a conversation that usually goes sideways, and the person you'll see there.
Ask what acting from love would look like there, just once: not a feeling to force but an act, like listening to the end, letting them go first, saying thank you and meaning it.
If you pray, rest in those three words from First John; if not, rest with the person's face.
